difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's theorem at source lines 915-917: the set of cuts has the Completeness Property, spelled out four lines earlier as the assertion that every non-empty set of cuts with an upper bound has a least upper bound (908-913). The 21-line proof constructs the candidate supremum as the union of the family and then discharges the three clauses of the definition of a cut for that union (923-936) before showing it is an upper bound and the least one (937-938). The definition of a cut is used clause by clause, and the minimality half has to pass between membership in the union and membership in a member of the family, so the argument is not a one-line consequence of the definitions.
